extracted.intended_audience: Organizations (generally charitable/nonprofit) and invited individuals seeking grants from the John Templeton Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying to the John Templeton Foundation via a required Online Funding Inquiry (OFI) and, if invited, a Full Proposal; includes eligibility, required materials, review process, timelines, and post-award agreement terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Funding Areas and Ventures
rubrics_metrics.description: We only fund projects aligned with our major Funding Areas and Ventures that advance the Foundation’s mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should read the Foundation’s Funding Areas and Ventures pages to ensure their project topic and goals clearly map to those priorities; proposals outside those areas will not be invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project type — generally discrete projects
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation generally funds discrete projects rather than ongoing operational support, program support, or donations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application process and forms are designed for discrete-project requests; do not use this process for requests that are essentially general operating support, donations, or broad program funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicant types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation funds charitable organizations (domestic and international). On rare occasions, and only by staff invitation, the Foundation may fund individuals or for‑profit companies doing charitable work consistent with tax‑exempt status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals or applicants representing for‑profit companies should not apply unsolicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑stage application process (OFI then Full Proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant consideration begins with a required Online Funding Inquiry (OFI). Full Proposals are by invitation only and follow an invited-notification process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must submit a complete OFI to be considered; only applicants who receive an invitation via email may submit a Full Proposal (the Full Proposal form appears in the Portal when invited).

rubrics_metrics.name: OFI required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OFI is a brief form requesting basic information: project title, requested amount, relevant dates, why the project is important, a brief description of activities, and information on people and organizations involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, concise answers to these items to enable staff to assess whether to invite a Full Proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: OFI evaluation criteria — strategic fit and potential for success
rubrics_metrics.description: Program staff review OFIs to determine whether a proposed project represents a realistic, strategic, and potentially successful opportunity to advance the Foundation’s philanthropic vision and fits within Funding Areas and donor intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff consider each OFI relative to limited resources and the quality of similar proposed projects; only the very strongest OFIs are invited to submit Full Proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing — Grant Calendar
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation reviews funding requests at specific times of year according to a Grant Calendar; Full Proposal invitations and review deadlines follow that calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Grant Calendar for notification dates and submission windows; Full Proposal invitations are sent in accordance with those dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: All materials must be submitted via the Templeton Portal
rubrics_metrics.description: All application materials are completed online in the Templeton Portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must create a Portal account and use the Portal for OFI submission and (if invited) Full Proposal submission; check the FAQ and Portal for instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Proposal content and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: A Full Proposal (by invitation) allows detailed project description with expanded field limits and places to upload required and optional files such as a budget, narrative description of activities, and supplemental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and upload budgets, narratives, and supporting documents as requested in the Full Proposal webform; the webform becomes available in the Portal the day the invitation notice is sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Proposal review process and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Proposals undergo a comprehensive review process that typically takes up to four and a half months and can include staff review, external review, proposal revisions, final review, and notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sequence and presence of intermediate steps are discretionary and nonlinear; applicants should expect a multi-stage review and potential requests for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff Review — completeness and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff review Full Proposals for completeness and accuracy and may request additional information, send the proposal for external review, or move it directly to the write-up stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide clarifications or administrative corrections if staff requests them; accurate, complete submissions reduce delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Review — use of external reviewers and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation may use external reviewers to evaluate proposals; reviewers offer information, suggestions, ideas, questions, and concerns to assess proposal quality and improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External reviewers are selected partly from applicant-suggested reviewers and partly by staff; typically at least two reviewers suggested by the applicant and one or more identified by the Foundation are invited. Reviewers’ identities are not shared with applicants. If staff deems external review unnecessary, proposals may skip this step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal revisions — notifications and required responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: If concerns, questions, or recommended improvements arise, the Foundation will notify applicants and request clarifications or revisions; applicants are expected to complete edits and resubmit by a specified due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should respond promptly and consult with Foundation staff if needed; failure to respond by the due date can result in the proposal being declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision authority and decision outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the Foundation’s Board of Trustees and its President have authority to approve funding; decisions are final and typically are: Approved as proposed, Declined as proposed, or Conditionally Approved pending acceptance of certain revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional approvals will include an email requesting final answers or revisions that must be accepted before funding is finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Agreement content and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are awarded through contractual Grant Agreements that detail general conditions (communications guidelines, compliance, prohibited uses), the approved budget, specific outputs and outcomes, and the payment and reporting schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation staff sends the Grant Agreement to the contract signatory designated in the Full Proposal; grantees must comply with the contractual terms.
